title: Medical AI Achieves Major Breakthrough: Research System AMIE Demonstrates Real-Time Clinical Video Consultation Capabilities for the First Time

content_html:
In real-world medical scenarios, doctors' diagnoses often rely not only on patients' verbal descriptions but also on keenly observing clues such as coughing sounds, abnormal gait, or facial expressions of discomfort. Recently, in the field of medical artificial intelligence, a research-oriented medical AI system called AMIE, developed jointly by Google Research and Google DeepMind, has achieved a technological breakthrough. For the first time, it has demonstrated expert-level capabilities in real-time clinical video consultations.

The system is built on the Gemini and Project Astra underlying architecture, using a multi-agent collaboration model. In the latest feature upgrade, AMIE can not only accurately interpret and combine visual and auditory cues but also flexibly guide virtual physical examinations and perform real-time diagnostic reasoning, making AI more similar to human experts in remote medical interactions.

In a recent simulated consultation randomized controlled study, researchers arranged volunteers playing patients to interact with primary care physicians and the AI system. Clinical evaluation results showed that professional evaluators gave positive feedback on AMIE's performance in several core clinical abilities, including the comprehensiveness of medical history collection, diagnostic accuracy, appropriateness of treatment plans, and overall communication quality. At the same time, the volunteers playing patients reported that compared to traditional text-based chat interactions, video consultations were more in line with clinical communication habits and provided a more friendly experience.

The development team pointed out that AMIE is still in the academic research stage, and before it can be responsibly deployed in real-world clinical settings, it still requires extensive rigorous validation and in-depth research. Nevertheless, this progress has already outlined a promising technical landscape for the future of intelligent development in the healthcare sector.

content_html_zh:
在现实的医疗场景中，医生的诊断往往不仅依赖于患者的口头描述，还依赖于敏锐观察咳嗽声音、异常步态或不适的面部表情等线索。 近日，在医疗人工智能领域，由谷歌研究院和谷歌DeepMind联合开发的名为AMIE的研究型医疗人工智能系统取得了技术突破。 首次展示了实时临床视频会诊的专家级能力。

该系统建立在Gemini和Project Astra底层架构之上，采用多智能体协作模型。 在最新的功能升级中，AMIE不仅可以准确解读和结合视觉和听觉线索，还可以灵活指导虚拟体检并进行实时诊断推理，使AI在远程医疗交互中更加类似于人类专家。

在最近的一项模拟咨询随机对照研究中，研究人员安排志愿者扮演患者，与初级保健医生和人工智能系统进行互动。 临床评估结果显示，专业评估人员对AMIE在病史收集的全面性、诊断准确性、治疗计划的适当性以及整体沟通质量等多项核心临床能力方面的表现给予了积极反馈。 同时，扮演患者的志愿者反映，相比传统的文字聊天互动，视频问诊更符合临床沟通习惯，提供更友好的体验。

开发团队指出，AMIE仍处于学术研究阶段，在实际临床环境中负责任地部署之前，仍需要广泛严格的验证和深入研究。 尽管如此，这一进展已经为医疗保健领域的智能发展的未来勾勒出了充满希望的技术前景。
